title: Post-Promotional Interest Calculation — Home Comfort Financing
content:
## Calculation

The post-promotional interest charge on a Home Comfort Financing account for a statement period is the post-promotional interest base, multiplied by the post-promotional rate and by the number of accrual days, divided by 100 and by 365, and rounded to the cent half up only at the end.

- **Accrual days.** The accrual days run from the day after the promotional end date when no interest charge has yet posted on the account, and otherwise from the day the previous interest charge posted, up to but not including the day this charge posts.
- **Post-promotional interest base.** The account balance on the day the charge posts.
- **Post-promotional rate.** The plan's post-promotional APR.

## Counting accrual days

| Account history | First accrual day | Last accrual day |
|---|---|---|
| no interest charge has posted on the account yet | the day after the promotional end date | the day before this charge posts |
| an interest charge has posted before | the day the previous interest charge posted | the day before this charge posts |

The day this charge posts is never an accrual day of this charge; it is the first accrual day of the next one.

## Worked example (hypothetical inputs)

An 18-Month 0% APR Equal Payment account's promotional end date is 31 March. Its post-promotional APR is 17.99 percent.

*First charge, posted 1 May.* No interest charge has posted yet, so the accrual days run from 1 April up to but not including 1 May: 30 days. With a balance of $2400.00 on 1 May: $2400.00 multiplied by 17.99 and by 30, divided by 100 and by 365, is $35.4871…, rounded half up to $35.49.

*Second charge, posted 1 June.* The previous interest charge posted on 1 May, so the accrual days run from 1 May up to but not including 1 June: 31 days. With a balance of $2365.51 on 1 June: $2365.51 multiplied by 17.99 and by 31, divided by 100 and by 365, is $36.1430…, rounded half up to $36.14.

## Rounding

Nothing is rounded along the way: the base, the rate and the day count are multiplied and divided in full, and only the final charge is rounded to the cent, half up.
